channel.title: iRecord Updates
channel.description: Updates for iRecord - Professional screen recording

item.title: Version 1.243.0
item.description:
What's New in 1.243.0

Fixed

  • Recording a window no longer leaves a black strip down one side of the video — for some windows, iRecord asked for a slightly wrong size before recording started, so the picture didn't quite fill the frame it was given and the leftover space showed up black in every frame. iRecord now checks the real size right before it starts and uses that instead. Full-screen recordings were never affected.
  • Deleting a Recording now really deletes it — the Recording disappeared from iRecord as it should, but an empty folder was left behind on your Mac every single time. They piled up quietly where your recordings are kept, and nothing ever cleared them. Nothing is left behind now.
  • A quiet hiccup could throw away your edits — when iRecord couldn't write one small companion file next to a take, it gave up on saving that Recording altogether, so the trims and splits you had just made were lost without a word. The companion file is now skipped if it can't be written, and your edits are saved either way.
  • Cropping your recording now fills the frame instead of leaving black bars — the trimmed picture used to play back inside the shape it had before you cropped it, so it looked smaller than the area you drew, with dark gaps where the trimmed edges used to be. The video now reshapes to exactly what you crop, in the editor and in the saved file.

item.title: Version 1.241.0
item.description:
What's New in 1.241.0

Added

  • Crop your screen recording right in the editor — say your window recording caught a row of browser tabs you'd rather not show. Open Edit and Crop is right there at the top; draw the area you want to keep and the rest is trimmed away in both the editor and your saved video.
  • A trash icon in the editor deletes a Recording without hunting for a right-click menu — that was the only way to delete a Recording from inside the editor before. Save Video and Edit also lost their text labels in favour of a tidier row of icons next to it (hover any of them for a reminder of what it does). Deleting still asks you to confirm first, since it can't be undone.
  • The timeline blocks show the sound in your recording — finding the pause where you stopped to think meant scrubbing back and forth watching the picture, because every block was a flat colour. Each block now draws the shape of its own sound, and a silence reads as a flat line along the bottom. Nothing about the recording changes; it is only easier to see where to cut.
  • The New Recording window says what is about to spoil the take — a cluttered desktop, a chat app that is one message away from showing on screen, a battery about to run out. These are easy to miss until you watch the recording back, so iRecord now lists them before you press Record. It only looks: nothing on your Mac is changed or switched off, and you can start recording whatever it says.
  • Re-record one part of a section without redoing the rest — if you had cut a section in two and wanted to redo only the second half, re-recording replaced both halves with the new take, so the first half stopped playing what you had recorded for it. Right-clicking a block now offers Re-record this Part alongside Re-record the Whole Section. The part you pick is the only one that changes, and every other block plays exactly what it played before.

Fixed

  • Your face and your voice are back in sync — the camera video started counting from the moment the camera woke up rather than from the moment the recording began, so everything it filmed played about a second early and your lips ran ahead of what you were saying. The camera now starts where the recording starts. If the camera takes a moment to wake up, that moment is simply blank instead of shifting the whole thing.
  • Choosing a window no longer offers you pieces of a window — some apps quietly keep extra windows open for their own toolbars and menus. These were listed alongside real windows, with nothing but the app's name on them, so two Chrome entries looked identical and picking the wrong one recorded a thin black strip instead of the page. Only real windows are offered now, and when two of them share a name the list shows their size so you can tell which is which.
  • The shortcut for stopping a recording actually stops it — the menu said ⌘⇧. stops recording, but it only worked while iRecord itself was in front, which is never the case while you are recording something else. It now works from any app, for as long as a recording is running.
  • Stopping from the floating bar takes one click, not two — clicking Stop while another app was in front spent the first click bringing iRecord forward, which on a full-screen recording put iRecord's own window into the video. The first click now stops the recording and iRecord stays out of the way.
  • The floating recording bar stays where you put it — dragging it out of the way worked until the next recording, when it went back to the top of the screen. It now reappears where you left it, including after you unplug an external display.
  • The file size shown before you save is now a limit, not a guess — the number on the Save screen was the most the video could weigh, but it was written as though it were the size you would get. Saved files often came in a lot smaller, because a recording of a mostly still screen compresses much further than a busy one. It now reads up to 31 MB, and the file you get is never bigger than that.
  • Re-recording a section could hide part of the take you just made — if you had split a section and then re-recorded it, only as much of the new take as the old one was long stayed on the timeline. Anything past that point was saved to disk but left out of your video, with nothing on screen to say so. The whole take now appears, and a note tells you it came out longer. If you had deliberately trimmed the end off a section, that trim is still respected.

item.title: Version 1.231.0
item.description:
What's New in 1.231.0

Changed

  • Notifications no longer appear in your recordings — a message or alert that arrived while you were recording the whole screen was captured along with everything else, and the only way to avoid it was to remember to turn notifications off first. Banners are now left out of the recording. You still see them on your screen; your viewers never do. Nothing about your Mac's settings is changed to make that happen, so there is nothing left switched off afterwards.

item.title: Version 1.230.0
item.description:
What's New in 1.230.0

Changed

  • Cursor zoom set to Auto now follows your pointer instead of staying zoomed in the whole time — Auto was meant to zoom while you are working and ease out when you stop, but it never did: it held the zoom from the first frame to the last. New recordings now zoom in while the pointer is being used and let go once it has been still for a second and a half. Recordings you already made are left exactly as they were and will save the same video as before; the panel shows them as Auto (always on) so you can see what they are doing, and picking any mode switches that recording over. Always follow gives you the old behaviour whenever you want it.

Fixed

  • Recording another section no longer stretches the zoom across it — if you had switched cursor zoom on and never dragged the ends of the zoom bar, it meant "to the end of the recording", so adding a section quietly extended it over footage you had not even watched yet. The zoom now stops where it did before, and the bar still drags out over the new section if that is what you wanted.
  • Turning on cursor zoom no longer makes the top of the window unclickable — with the zoom switched on, Home and the recording's name stopped responding to clicks, which looked like the app had frozen. The zoomed video was covering them without being visible there. The same thing happened at the 150% and 200% preview sizes with the zoom switched off.
  • The pointer trail no longer drifts out of step after a pause — the trail behind the zoom effect kept being recorded while a recording was paused, so everything after the pause was stamped as happening later than it did — by however long you were paused, for the rest of the recording. The zoom then followed your pointer from the wrong moment. It now pauses with the recording.
  • A recording tells you when the camera didn't record — if the camera was switched on but produced nothing, iRecord saved the recording, kept a pointer to a camera file it had just deleted, and said nothing at all. The section then opened with no camera and no explanation. It now says so as soon as the recording stops, and the recording itself is saved either way.
  • An older recording keeps its edits after you record another section into it — recordings made by early versions of iRecord stored their takes differently. Adding one new section to such a recording made the app stop seeing the takes on all the older sections: their trims and splits were undone, Delete Section did nothing on them, and the file was rewritten every time you opened the app. All of it works again, and the edits stay exactly as you left them.
  • A future update can no longer wipe the trims and splits you have already made — because of the way edits were read back from disk, anything new added to them in a later version would have quietly replaced every existing edit with an untouched recording, with no warning and no way back. Edits are now read piece by piece, so new features can be added around yours without disturbing them.
  • The zoom you set on part of a recording now saves where you put it — if you dragged the zoom bar to cover just one stretch of your recording, the saved video ignored that and switched the zoom on at some other moment inside every section instead. What you see in the editor and what comes out of Save Video now match. Only recordings where you moved the zoom bar were affected.
  • The zoom bar's edges follow your pointer — dragging either end of the zoom bar made it race away from the pointer and slam into the end of the timeline, so the range was almost impossible to set. It now moves with your pointer.
  • The zoom no longer flickers where two sections meet — in the saved video a zoom that carried across a cut dropped out and eased back in at every cut. It now holds steady across the cut, the way the editor always showed it.
  • Takes are numbered in the order you recorded them — re-recording a section could give the new take a number already in use, so the take list showed two takes with the same name. Each take now gets the next free number.

item.title: Version 1.228.0
item.description:
What's New in 1.228.0

Added

  • A recording that doesn't finish is offered back to you next time you open iRecord — if the app or your Mac stopped unexpectedly mid-recording, the file used to be unplayable and iRecord never mentioned it existed. Recordings are now written so that everything up to the last few seconds survives, and the next launch asks whether you want it back. Choosing to discard keeps the files for a week in case you didn't mean it.
  • The recording indicator shows how much is already safe on disk — a second line under the timer, so you can see the recording is being written and not just counting. For the first few seconds it reads --:--, because nothing has been written yet and saying 00:00 looked like something had gone wrong.

Fixed

  • The recording timer no longer freezes while a menu is open — opening a menu, or dragging the recording indicator around the screen, stopped the clock for as long as you held it there, and then it jumped forward when you let go. The recording itself was always fine; only the counter stalled. It now keeps time from the clock rather than by counting its own ticks, so it stays right even when the Mac is busy.
  • The mouse pointer is still tracked while a menu is open — the same fault affected the pointer trail behind the zoom effect, which stopped being recorded for as long as any menu was down. That left a gap at the exact moment the pointer was most likely to be moving.
  • Recordings you add or remove in Finder now show up on the Home screen — the list was read once when iRecord started, so a Recording folder you deleted in Finder kept appearing, and one you moved in never showed at all until you quit and reopened the app. Home now checks for changes when you go back to it and when you switch back to iRecord.
  • A recording that didn't finish now says when it stopped, not just when it started — the offer to bring it back gave the length and the start time, so there was no way to tell a recording that ended early from one that ran until the Mac did.
  • Running out of disk space mid-recording now stops and saves instead of silently breaking the take — the check only ran before you pressed Record, so a long recording could outrun the space it started with and end up damaged with nothing said. iRecord now warns while there is still room to free some up, and if space runs out anyway it stops and saves what you have.
  • A take with no picture no longer breaks the whole recording — the app used to pick a take that saved sound but no video, and then your video wouldn't save at all. Those takes are skipped now, and a recording already stuck this way fixes itself when you open it. Nothing is deleted.
  • The camera stays in step with an iPhone or iPad recording after the cable is knocked — when the connection dropped and came back, the app trimmed the dead air out of the phone recording but not out of the camera in the corner. Your face then ran behind your voice for the rest of the take, by however long the cable was out. The camera now pauses with the recording and picks up in the right place.
  • Recordings on the home screen no longer sit on top of each other — each card was being stretched to the size of the picture inside it, so they came out at different widths and overlapped their neighbours. Every recording now gets an evenly sized card with the picture trimmed to fit.
